newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -July 25.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -July 25.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

HAMBURG - Radio Marketing Service GmbH & Co. KG (RMS), a media buyer, shows stronger gross income for 1996 than the industry average. The agency's gross income reached 923 million marks ($503.2 million), an increase of 2.5 percent, making it the largest media buyer for radio ads. (Reuter)

FRANFURT - Germany's main tourism agency, Deutschland Tourismus Marketing (DTM), reports a positive response to its first campaign promoting holidays in Germany. Travel agency and travel companies were pleased with the campaign, DTM says. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Bavarian media tycoon Leo Kirch, one of German television industry's most guarded figures, is lifting the veil of secrecy that shrouds his media empire. Kirch's seven managing directors have begun courting journalists in what they described as the first step of a new policy of openness aimed at improving what they see as a skewed picture of the man and his media
enterprise. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

FRANKFURT - Rallying stock markets pump profits into Germany's top banks in the first six months but investors are paying far more attention to the prospect of further mega-mergers. This week's earnings releases by Deutsche Bank AG , Commerzbank AG and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG have been completely overshadowed by Monday's news of a Bavarian merger that will transform Germany's bank landscape. (Reuter)
HERZOGENAURACH - Sportswear group Puma AG expects sales growth below 10 percent this year after turnover climbed six percent in the first half. (Reuter)

MUNICH - German luxury carmaker Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG (BMW) says deliveries climbed 10 percent in the first half of 1997 to around 350,000 units and it grabbed a larger share of the German car market. (Reuter)
METZINGEN - Fashion group Hugo Boss AG forecasts at least a 10-percent increase in sales this year although the pace of growth will slow in the second half. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Rolls-Royce, a badge of wealth and privilege on four wheels, hopes to be a bit more politically correct with its first totally new model in nearly two decades that is due by the turn of the century. Rolls-Royce Motor Cars Limited chief executive Graham Morris says he wants the British carmaker's new model to have "more socially acceptable shapes". (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
BERLIN - Klaus Schaefer is named chairman for sales and marketing at Brau und Brunnen AG brewery, effective immediately.
He was previously on the company's advisory board. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Creative director Ilona Klueck leaves Scholz & Friends in Hamburg for Ogilvy & Mather in Frankfurt. She was responsible for the international West cigarettes account at Scholz & Friends. (Reuter)
